note: Hand-curated themed tours. Each stop resolves through scripts/tours/build-tours.ts: landmarkId (landmarks.json), osm (click-poi-info.json, an OSM extract), orientation (orientation-pois.json name + optional near hint) or street (streets.json, nearest point to near). 'why' is one sentence taken from 'source'; food and cafe tours quote only what the cited guide says and are volatile.

tours.title: Jewish Amsterdam
tours.blurb: From the Anne Frank House across the old Jewish quarter to the theatre the occupiers turned into a deportation centre.

stops.name: Anne Frank House
stops.why: Anne Frank hid from Nazi persecution with her family in the rear of this Prinsengracht building during the German occupation.

stops.name: Jodenbreestraat
stops.why: The southern part of Sint Antoniesbreestraat came to be called Jodenbreestraat, 'Jewish Broad Street', in the later 17th century, after Jewish refugees from Portugal and Spain settled around it.

stops.name: De Dokwerker
stops.why: Mari Andriessen's statue on Jonas Daniël Meijerplein commemorates the February Strike of 1941 against the persecution of the Jews.

stops.name: Portugese Synagoge
stops.why: The Esnoga of Amsterdam's Sephardi community was completed in 1675 and is still in use.

stops.name: Joods Museum
stops.why: The only museum in the Netherlands dedicated to Jewish history; since 1987 it has occupied four former synagogues.

stops.name: Nationaal Holocaust Namenmonument
stops.why: Since 2021 the national Holocaust memorial, it names the roughly 102,000 Jews from the Netherlands who were deported and murdered.

stops.name: Hollandsche Schouwburg
stops.why: The occupiers made this theatre a Jewish theatre in 1941 and then used it as a deportation centre.

tours.title: Golden Age canal ring
tours.blurb: Along the 17th-century ring from the Westerkerk to the Amstel: merchant houses, the Golden Bend and the Skinny Bridge.

stops.name: Westerkerk
stops.why: Designed by Hendrick de Keyser and inaugurated in 1631, it is one of the first churches built for Protestant worship.

stops.name: Huis Bartolotti
stops.why: Built around 1617 at Herengracht 170-172 for Willem van den Heuvel, who took the name Bartolotti to inherit his uncle's fortune.

stops.name: Golden Bend
stops.why: The stretch of Herengracht between Leidsestraat and Vijzelstraat, dug after 1663 with wider lots that drew the city's richest residents.

stops.name: Museum Van Loon
stops.why: A canal house on the Keizersgracht named after the Van Loon family, who lived in it from the 19th century.

stops.name: Magere Brug
stops.why: The 'Skinny Bridge' crosses the Amstel at Kerkstraat; the present white wooden bridge of 1934 replaced a 13-arched bridge of 1691.

tours.title: Art museums
tours.blurb: Rembrandt's house to Museumplein by way of the Amstel and the Keizersgracht.

stops.name: Rembrandthuis
stops.why: Rembrandt lived and worked in this Jodenbreestraat house from 1639 until it was auctioned in 1658.

stops.name: H'ART Museum
stops.why: The Amstel-side art museum was a satellite of the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg until it cut ties after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

stops.name: Foam
stops.why: Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam on the Keizersgracht shows four photography exhibitions at any time.

stops.name: Rijksmuseum
stops.why: The national museum of Dutch art and history, founded in The Hague in 1798 and moved to Amsterdam in 1808.

stops.name: Moco Museum
stops.why: An independent museum of modern and contemporary art that opened on Museumplein in 2016.

stops.name: Van Gogh Museum
stops.why: Dedicated to Vincent van Gogh and his contemporaries, it opened on 2 June 1973 in a building by Gerrit Rietveld.

stops.name: Stedelijk Museum
stops.why: The city's museum of modern and contemporary art and design, in a 19th-century building by Adriaan Willem Weissman.

tours.title: Churches and towers
tours.blurb: The spires and wall towers that pin the old city's skyline, from the Westerkerk to the Munttoren.

stops.name: Westerkerk
stops.why: Inaugurated in 1631 to a design by Hendrick de Keyser, it is still the largest church built for Protestants in the Netherlands.

stops.name: Nieuwe Kerk
stops.why: The 15th-century church on Dam Square beside the Royal Palace became Dutch Reformed in 1578.

stops.name: Oude Kerk
stops.why: Amsterdam's oldest parish church and oldest building, founded around 1213 and consecrated in 1306.

stops.name: Schreierstoren
stops.why: A defensive tower of 1487 from the medieval city wall, from which Henry Hudson set out on his voyage to North America.

stops.name: Montelbaanstoren
stops.why: Built in 1516 as part of the city walls; Hendrick de Keyser's decorative top was added in 1606.

stops.name: Zuiderkerk
stops.why: The 17th-century church of the Nieuwmarkt area played a part in Rembrandt's life and was painted by Claude Monet.

stops.name: Munttoren
stops.why: A remnant of the medieval Regulierspoort, rebuilt after a 1618 fire with a spire by Hendrick de Keyser; coins were minted beside it in 1672.

tours.title: Markets
tours.blurb: Five street markets from the Jordaan to Oost: flowers, flea market, food and fabric.

stops.name: Noordermarkt
stops.why: The Jordaan square holds a Monday market and a popular organic farmers' market on Saturdays.

stops.name: Bloemenmarkt
stops.why: A floating flower market on the Singel between Muntplein and Koningsplein, dating back to 1862.

stops.name: Albert Cuypmarkt
stops.why: The De Pijp street market became official in 1905 and a six-day daytime market in 1912; it is named after the painter Albert Cuyp.

stops.name: Waterlooplein
stops.why: The square was made in 1882 by filling in two canals; Jewish traders were moved here, and after the war the market became a flea market.

stops.name: Dappermarkt
stops.why: The city made Dapperstraat in Oost an official market street in 1910.

tours.title: Ice cream
tours.blurb: Ice cream parlours named in published Amsterdam guides, from Westerpark to De Pijp. Shops change: check before you go.

stops.name: Doardi
stops.why: I amsterdam's ice cream guide lists Doardi at Van Limburg Stirumstraat 15 and says Westerpark is best experienced with one of its ice creams in hand.

stops.name: Monte Pelmo
stops.why: I amsterdam describes this 2e Anjeliersdwarsstraat parlour as a family-owned ice cream institution in the heart of the Jordaan.

stops.name: IJssalon Tofani
stops.why: Your Little Black Book's ice cream guide lists Tofani at Kloveniersburgwal 16, near Nieuwmarkt.

stops.name: Miuz
stops.why: I amsterdam lists Miuz at Ferdinand Bolstraat 4 and notes its gelato is slow-churned and kept in covered containers.

stops.name: Massimo Gelato
stops.why: I amsterdam calls Massimo, listed at Van Ostadestraat 147 among others, one of the most authentic Italian gelaterias in the city.

tours.title: Pizza
tours.blurb: Pizzerias picked by I amsterdam and Time Out, from the Haarlemmerdijk to De Pijp. Shops change: check before you go.

stops.name: De Pizzabakkers
stops.why: I amsterdam's pizza guide lists the Haarlemmerdijk 128 branch of De Pizzabakkers for its oven-baked thin, crusty pizza.

stops.name: Yam-Yam
stops.why: Time Out Amsterdam names Yam-Yam as tying for the best pizza in town.

stops.name: nNea
stops.why: I amsterdam lists nNea at Bilderdijkstraat 92 for its light Neapolitan-style crusts with seasonal toppings.

stops.name: Pizza Beppe
stops.why: I amsterdam lists Pizza Beppe, with a branch at Nassaukade 379, as the first in the Netherlands accepted by the guardians of pizza authenticity.

stops.name: Mangia Pizza
stops.why: I amsterdam lists Mangia at Vijzelgracht 33 and says its pizzas have taken the Amsterdam pizza world by storm.

stops.name: Renato's Pizzeria
stops.why: I amsterdam lists Renato's at Karel du Jardinstraat 32 for Roman-style bases since 2013.

tours.title: Brown cafés
tours.blurb: Old wood-panelled bars from the Jordaan to the eastern docks, as described by I amsterdam. Opening hours change: check before you go.

stops.name: Café Chris
stops.why: I amsterdam lists Café Chris at Bloemstraat 42 and says it opened as a beer house in 1624, a date other guides dispute.

stops.name: Café 't Smalle
stops.why: I amsterdam says a liqueur distillery opened here on the Egelantiersgracht around 1780.

stops.name: Café Hoppe
stops.why: I amsterdam lists Hoppe on the Spui and says it has been pouring jenever for 348 years.

stops.name: In 't Aepjen
stops.why: I amsterdam dates the Zeedijk 1 building to 1475 and says its annexe became a tavern in the 17th century.

stops.name: Café De Druif
stops.why: I amsterdam says the Rapenburgerplein café has been serving liquor since 1631.
